title: Oracle C2M Batch Scheduling & Thread-Pool Management
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Oracle Utilities C2M + WebLogic 14c administration; middleware/database/integration work, production-impact care).

Oracle Utilities C2M/CC&B/MDM + WebLogic 14c authored from Oracle's official product + OUAF docs; version-specific details (C2M 25.4/min v2.9, WebLogic 14c) cited or flagged 'verify for your version'; My-Oracle-Support-gated patches/notes are pointed to, not reproduced. Automation is WLST (Jython)/shell/SQL, not PowerShell.
hook: Run C2M batch reliably — threadpools, schedules, and monitoring
problem: C2M does its heavy lifting in batch — billing, meter reads, and more — and batch that's mis-scheduled or under-resourced quietly breaks the business. This solution configures and manages C2M batch: threadpool workers, batch scheduling and dependencies, DBMS scheduler/enterprise scheduler integration, and batch monitoring — so jobs run on time and complete, pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the C2M batch architecture: threadpool workers, batch control, scheduling, dependencies, and monitoring.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (C2M environment, threadpool config, scheduler, DB access).
Implementation Guide — exact steps to configure named threadpool workers, set up batch scheduling and dependencies, integrate the scheduler, and validate throughput and completion, pilot-first.

5 automation scripts (WLST/Jython, shell & SQL) — environment/config discovery, per-node validation, a health/coverage report, safe remediation (dry-run by default), and a scope/target helper — authentic to C2M & WebLogic administration.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (threadpools up, jobs complete, no backlog) plus Best Practices for batch sizing and scheduling.
short: Configure and manage C2M batch — threadpool workers, scheduling and dependencies, scheduler integration, and monitoring — so jobs run on time and complete, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
